item.description: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Alabama QB Keelon Russell upgraded to probable for Vanderbilt battle appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Alabama football is preparing to face Vanderbilt as the Crimson Tide look to improve their 7-2 overall record and maintain their position in the SEC race. However, quarterback Keelon Russell’s availability had emerged as a major concern heading into the Week 11 matchup. Now, Alabama fans have received some encouraging news as the team gets a significant boost regarding his status. Pete Nakos of On3 reported that Russell has been upgraded to probable for the upcoming game. “Alabama QB Keelon Russell is probable for this week against Vanderbilt,” Nakos wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Alongside Russell, cornerback Zabien Brown, running back EJ Crowell, offensive lineman William Sanders and defensive back Chuck McDonald have also been listed as probable for the game. Meanwhile, several other Crimson Tide players have been ruled out of the game. Russell sustained an ankle injury in the third quarter against LSU and briefly headed to the medical tent as backup quarterback Austin Mack prepared to step in. However, the signal-caller managed to return to the game and delivered an impressive performance, helping Alabama complete its comeback victory . Russell finished the game with 17 completions on 24 attempts for 206 passing yards and three touchdowns. He also contributed 25 rushing yards on eight carries while protecting the football and avoiding any turnovers. So far this season, Russell has thrown for 2,263 yards, 18 touchdowns and five interceptions. The young quarterback has also demonstrated his dual-threat ability on the ground, recording 276 rushing yards and five touchdowns. For now, Russell’s probable designation for the upcoming game represents an encouraging development for Alabama. However, the coaching staff will continue monitoring his recovery before making a final decision on his availability. If Russell is ultimately unable to play, Mack is expected to take over the starting quarterback duties and make his first career start for Alabama. However, the backup quarterback could face a significant challenge against Vanderbilt, making Russell’s potential return particularly important for the Crimson Tide. item.title: Workaholic with a tattooed throat – meet The Merthyr Mexican
item.description: Gavin Gwynne has held Welsh, British, Commonwealth and European lightweight titles as well as the WBA International Super Lightweight belt [Getty Images] You can't miss Gavin Gwynne. It might be the giant sombrero that the rugged lightweight wears to the ring, in keeping with his moniker of 'The Merthyr Mexican'. Or it will be the roaring lion prominently inked on his throat that invites the second glances and stares. Lately, though, the proud valleys fighter is showing there are more reasons for people to take note. Having already won British, Commonwealth and European titles, his upset of previously 16-fight unbeaten Khaleel Majid in May won him the WBA international belt at the weight above - and shot the 36-year-old up the rankings. Now, as he prepares to face Manchester's Zelfa Barrett for the WBA intercontinental lightweight title at Wembley Arena on Saturday, 14 November, Gwynne knows he has a chance to be known for more than a nickname and a neck tattoo. "I'm 36 but just feel like I'm getting better," Gwynne told BBC Sport Wales. "Just look at Anthony Cacace, he was 35 when he won his world title. That's what I want. I want these big fights, even if I can get a title shot. "All I have to do is win this fight and it pushes me in contention. It's must-win." Facing Pacquiao in Cardiff would be honour for Cordina Price rules out Shields but hints at big showdown Price to defend world titles against Kotaskova on BBC Gwynne believes it is possible too, having already achieved more than he thought he could when he swapped carpentry and building sites to go full-time just a few years ago. Maybe it will redress a balance, Gwynne feeling he has not got the credit his 'fight all-comers' mantra has deserved. Sharing a gym with one former world champion, Joe Cordina, and preparing for Barrett with tough sparring sessions with another in Lee Selby, Gwynne suggests he has even been overlooked in his homeland. "Maybe it's because I haven't got one of those eye-catching styles," he wondered aloud. "But if you watch me, I'm always giving my all and for 12 rounds I'll give anyone nightmares." The stories behind the nickname and the neck tattoo Gwynne admits former world title challenger Zelfa Barrett will be "a step up in class" when they meet on Saturday, 14 November [Getty Images] There are a fair few fighters who will attest to that, with even his most recent defeat – in November 2024 to the undefeated Cameron Vuong – booed by the crowd who seemed to disagree with the judges' scorecards. In the first half, the Bulls shot over 80% from the field and the 3-point line, but finished at 57.9% from the field and 51.7% from beyond the arc. The Bulls were outscored 34-19 in the 3rd quarter as Victor Wembanyama, De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and company took advantage of Chicago’s carelessness with the ball. Jalen Smith led the Bulls in scoring with 23 points and shooting 8-for-9 from the field. Nic Claxton came off the bench and added 17 points along with six rebounds. Wilson played 15 minutes before he left the game and finished with 15 points. Before the game, Wilson was listed as questionable due to right hip soreness. item.description: Swansea won seven of their first 10 league games this season, but managed only once victory in the next five [Huw Evans Picture Agency] At the 10-game landmark in 2026-27, Swansea City were basking in the glory of the club's best start to a league campaign in more than a century. Five matches later, the mood is less buoyant but the outlook - as things stand - remains bright. Swansea banked 23 from their first 10 league fixtures of the campaign, the club's best return – when counting three points for a win in every season – at that stage since 1923. A review of how things were going after victory at Millwall a month ago – which left Swansea two points clear at the top of the table - would have struggled to find many faults. Since then, however, Vitor Matos' team have hit problems. A run of four defeats – and 11 goals conceded along the way – in five games has served as a reminder of how difficult it will be to sustain a push for automatic promotion in a division packed with contenders. Nevertheless, Swansea remain in the logjam at the top-end of the table, meaning dreams of doing something special this season remain intact. Swansea are in the Championship for a ninth successive season. In the past five of those, mid-table has become home. For Matos, in his first full campaign at the helm, the challenge is to ensure the Swans are playing for something come next spring. With the teams finishing seventh and eighth reaching the play-offs for the first time this season, a host of second-tier clubs started out in August believing opportunity knocks. Swansea were among those eyeing a top-eight place, even if they have not finished higher than 11th since they said farewell to Premier League parachute payments in 2021. Yet the form of the first two months of the campaign led some to believe Matos' squad could contend for the top two rather than the top eight. Swansea are down to sixth in the table on the back of last weekend's defeat at Birmingham City, who are the latest leaders in a fiercely contested race at the top. With only three points between them and the Blues, Swansea are right in the mix with almost a third of the season played. item.title: Mike Brown slams the referees for letting Jalen Brunson's defenders get away with fouls
item.description: Mike Brown slams the referees for letting Jalen Brunson's defenders get away with fouls originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks suffered a tough loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night. The defending champions struggled, especially in the second leg of a back-to-back. Still, the Knicks could have won; they only lost by eight points. Brunson led the charge for the champions with 27 points, but he never got to the free-throw line in his 35 minutes on the floor. Mike Brown is frustrated with the referees not calling fouls The Knicks are quite reliant on Brunson dominating on offense. He is one of the most unique point guards in the league because he thrives with posting up in the paint and living in that part of the court. Physicality often plays a role in his game, so he gets fouled quite often. However, that did not happen for the Knicks because he did not get a single trip to the free-throw line, which frustrated Knicks head coach Mike Brown. MORE: The Knicks' problem involves Jalen Brunson and Mikal Bridges It is difficult to build rhythm without going to the free-throw line. Brunson still did well as the star player, scoring 27 points, but free throws would have changed the game for the Knicks. "The possession game, and we lost in every category. They had 14 more free-throw attempts than us... Jalen played almost 35 minutes; he had zero free-throw attempts. That's pretty alarming. I'm not sure how or why it was that way. That's not why we lost the game, but you hope you get a better whistle," Brown said after the Knicks' loss to the Cavaliers . Moving forward, the Knicks will want to attack the basket even more to draw more fouls. However, Brunson will continue to play his game, and by doing so, he will naturally draw fouls to build his rhythm and get easier shots. item.title: Wembanyama leads Spurs to 10th straight NBA win
item.description: San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama shoots over Jalen Smith in the Spurs' NBA winover the Chicago Bulls (Michael Reaves) The San Antonio Spurs rallied from 22 points down to beat the Chicago Bulls 124-119 on Wednesday, notching a 10th straight NBA win and keeping the pressure on the league-leading Los Angeles Lakers. The Lakers improved their league-best record to 11-2 -- half a game ahead of the 10-2 Spurs atop the West -- with a 123-112 victory over the Bucks in Milwaukee. Luka Doncic scored 32 points but limped out late in the fourth quarter after rolling his right ankle. In Chicago, Victor Wembanyama poured in 32 points to lead seven Spurs players who scored double figures. But San Antonio had to claw back from a 22-point first-half deficit against the lowly Bulls -- who dropped their eighth straight. Chicago's 41-first-quarter points were the most allowed in the opening period by the Spurs this season. They limited Wembanyama early, but they couldn't keep it up. He finished an efficient 13-of-18 from the floor with nine rebounds, two steals and five blocked shots, and the Spurs erased a 14-point half-time deficit in the first four minutes of the third quarter. The Lakers led most of the way in Milwaukee, where they also faced a struggling team in the Bucks. "(It) could have easily been a trap game for us," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "So I appreciate the way we handled the first half and then to build that lead in the third quarter and through the early part of the fourth was excellent." Redick said he thought Doncic's injury was "just a light tweak." Teammate Austin Reaves will require further tests on a left heel injury suffered in the third quarter when he landed awkwardly. The Cleveland Cavaliers, led by 32 points from James Harden and 23 from Donovan Mitchell, beat the defending champion New York Knicks 115-107 at Madison Square Garden. The Cavs got off to a hot start and led by 12 in the first quarter before hanging on for the win. The Knicks managed to tie the score four times in the second half but never took the lead. Peyton Watson's fourth block with 33.7 seconds left led to a thunderous dunk from Cavs center Jarrett Allen that pushed the lead to seven points and essentially sealed the win. - Celtics overcome Raptors - Boston's Jayson Tatum made the go-ahead free throws with 25.2 seconds left as the Celtics rallied to beat the Raptors 98-93 in Toronto. Boston trailed by as many as 22 but stepped it up defensively in the second half to notch a fifth straight win, one night after an emotional win over ex-Celtic Jaylen Brown and the 76ers in Philadelphia. "You know, a four-game road trip is tough, especially a back-to-back, how late we got in last night," Tatum said. "It was ugly, but I'll take it," added Tatum, who led all scorers with 24 and added seven rebounds and eight assists. item.title: No. 16 Eastern New Mexico Greyhounds Ready to Tip Off Third Season Under Daven Võ
item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) - Optimism is building in Portales as the Eastern New Mexico Men's Basketball Team prepares to tip off its season on Friday, entering the year ranked No. 16 nationally in NCAA Division II. The upcoming campaign marks the third season under head coach Daven Võ, who returns a talented core from a Greyhound squad that won 26 games last season. Võ says having eight returning players, including key contributors Austin Abrams and Maurice Austin, gives his team a strong foundation heading into the new season. "I feel great in the fact that we have got eight guys, a majority of the team coming back from a 26-win season," Võ said. "It feels really good to have my point guard and one of our leading scorers, Austin Abrams and Maurice Austin." The Greyhounds have also added new talent to the roster, with Võ pointing to the leadership of his returning players as a major factor in helping the newcomers adjust and find their roles. Eastern New Mexico will open the season with a challenging matchup against New Mexico Highlands on Friday. The Cowboys, coached by former University of New Mexico assistant Scott Waterman. Võ points to the program's 2024 Lone Star Conference Tournament championship banner as a reminder of what the team hopes to accomplish. "Right there, right up there is the 2024 LSC Tournament Championship. Brent Owen in his last year got that, and we want to hang a banner," Võ said. "We want to either win a regular season championship, a conference tournament championship, a regional championship, or a national championship." For Võ, the goal goes beyond winning games. He wants this group to accomplish something that will leave a lasting mark on the program. "That's something that we talk about quite a bit, is winning a championship and doing something lasting," Võ said. item.title: The CFP’s 24-Team Expansion Raises New Financial Questions For College Football
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - JANUARY 08: Najee Harris #22 of the Alabama Crimson Tide runs the ball during the second half against the Georgia Bulldogs in the CFP National Championship at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 8, 2018 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox - Remote/Getty Images) Getty Images The College Football Playoff doubled its field, and ESPN is paying more, but the new money after the loss of conference title games is thin. Schools are also betting that fans who didn’t want this will keep watching. College football’s postseason will grow from 12 teams to 24 in 2027, and the check is smaller than the headline suggests. The College Football Playoff and ESPN finalized the deal on Monday, and the CFP did not disclose financial terms. ESPN reported that the network will pay an average of $345 million more per year for five years, about $1.7 billion in all. That sits on top of the roughly $1.3 billion a year ESPN already pays under a six-year, $7.8 billion contract that runs through the 2031 season. The Money Left After The Title Games Go The four Power 4 conferences each said this season’s championship game will be its last. They needed the December calendar space, and the games carried real money. People familiar with the talks put the combined value of those games at about $250 million. ESPN holds the rights to the ACC, Big 12 and SEC games and gets about $140 million a year back from the cancellations, according to its reporting. That cuts its real cost for the new games to roughly $205 million. Fox, which owns the Big Ten game, is expected to get back about $50 million. After the $200 million already flowing to conferences for those title game rights, the surplus is about $145 million. That works out to a little more than $2 million per school per year, though the split will not be equal. Big Ten and SEC programs would gain $2.5 million to $3 million annually, while ACC and Big 12 programs would gain $1 million to $1.5 million. For comparison, last season conferences received $4 million for each team that made the playoff and another $4 million for each team that reached the quarterfinals. ESPN bid on 10 of the 12 new games, so $205 million in net cost is about $20.5 million per game. Why Schools Took A Smaller Payoff Roster spending has climbed to tens of millions of dollars at many programs in the revenue-sharing era. Leaders argued that more schools need a credible shot at the postseason to justify that spending. Georgia coach Kirby Smart raised concerns about finances at the SEC spring meetings in May. He said he was “ really more worried about the financial burden that we’re under right now of paying for all of the athletic department. ” What Fans Told The CFP In August, the CFP commissioned a Nielsen Sports survey . item.title: Lakers Make Pair of Roster Moves to Shake Up End of Bench
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers signed center Carson Cooper to a two-way contract on Tuesday. In a corresponding move, the Lakers waived 7-footer Lawson Lovering. Cooper comes over from the Memphis Grizzlies, filling the third two-way slot on the Lakers alongside forward Arthur Kaluma and guard Chris Manon. Los Angeles is currently 10-2 and on a six-game win streak . More About Cooper Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Cooper is a 6-foot-11 big man with little NBA experience. The Grizzlies signed the undrafted rookie out of Michigan State to a two-way deal this offseason. Cooper played for the Spartans all four years in college, peaking in his final year to create some league buzz. He averaged 11.1 points and 7.1 rebounds per game as a senior, adding one block in 26.7 minutes. He shot 58.4 percent from the field and 40 percent from beyond the arc, albeit on just five attempts. There is not a ton of floor-stretching potential there right now. Cooper's profile is more similar to Walker Kessler's , which may be why the Lakers were inclined to sign him as a depth piece with room to grow. The 22-year-old played just one game with the Grizzlies this season, posting one point, two rebounds, and one assist in three minutes against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 31. Cooper featured sparingly in preseason, topping out at 15 minutes in his first of three games, where he scored 8 points and added four rebounds on 2-for-3 shooting. What's Next For Lovering Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Lovering is a second-year undrafted center out of Utah. He spent last season with the Grizzlies, playing mostly for their G League affiliate, the Memphis Hustle, before the Lakers recruited him this offseason. The 23-year-old appeared twice for the Lakers, both late in already decided games. He impressed in the G League last year, earning himself some playing time with the Grizzlies. Lovering averaged 8.9 points and 7.8 rebounds in 13 games with the Hustle. In his second, and last, NBA game with the Grizzlies, he posted 11 points, 11 rebounds, three assists, one block, and one steal in 32 minutes on Feb. 20 against the Utah Jazz, shooting 5-for-8 from the field. Lovering put enough on tape to prompt the Lakers to want to give Lovering a shot. However, the Purple and Gold chose to go with Cooper's upside as a younger and more accomplished college prospect. Lovering will now look for a new home and may find one soon in a league that's always searching for center depth.
